chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ḥannān ibn Sadīr, that ʿAbbād al-Makkī said:

Sufyān al-Thawrī said to me: I see that you hold a position with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, so ask him about a man who committed zina while he is ill; if the hadd is carried out upon him, they fear that he may die—what do you say about him?

He said: So I asked him, and he said to me: “Is this question from yourself, or did someone instruct you to ask about it?” He said: I said: Sufyān al-Thawrī instructed me to ask you about it. He said: Then he said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was brought a very old man whose abdomen had become swollen and the veins of his thighs had become visible, and he had committed zina with a sick woman. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ordered, and a palm-branch stalk containing one hundred twigs was brought. He struck him with one strike, and he struck her with one strike, then let them go on their way.”
And that is His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “And take in your hand a bundle, then strike with it, and do not break your oath.”

key_terms.رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the cited precedent
key_terms.شِمْرَاخٍ: a twig or strand on a branch
key_terms.ضِغْثًا: a bundle of stalks or twigs

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on administering the hadd for zina to a sick person who may die from the punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for carrying out the hadd in a case where the offenders are physically ill and a normal punishment may cause death. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام cites an action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and relates it to a Qur'anic expression, indicating a mitigated form of implementation in severe weakness while preserving the legal penalty.
